findings.evidence: Determinacy.lean:83-89 `ae_eq_of_forall_mellinMomentH_eq (h₁ : IntegrableOn ...) (h₂ : IntegrableOn ...)`; Determinacy.lean:164-171 the existential has only `Assumptions M₁ ∧ Assumptions M₂ ∧ moment-agreement ∧ ¬ae-eq ∧ DGLAP`; `GPD.Assumptions` (Basic.lean:52-55) postulates only support/skewness vanishing, so integrability does not follow from it — a point the file's own docstring at lines 71-72 makes.
findings.fix: Add the two integrability clauses to the existential, e.g. `IntegrableOn (fun x => M₁.H i x xi t) (Icc (-1) 1) ∧ IntegrableOn (fun x => M₂.H i x xi t) (Icc (-1) 1)` for each `i xi t`; for `Model.zero` this is `integrable_zero`, and for `polynomialModel` it is `((p.continuous.integrableOn_Icc).indicator measurableSet_Icc).mono_set (Icc_subset_Icc (by norm_num) le_rfl)`-style one-liner, since `H` is `(Icc 0 1).indicator (p.eval ·)` at physical skewness. (The `Polynomial ℝ` analogue in `MomentDeterminacy.lean:154` needs nothing: `p.continuous.integrableOn_Icc` is immediate and the file already uses it at line 105.)
findings.issue: `exists_models_forall_le_mellinMomentH_eq_and_H_not_ae_eq` asserts no integrability of `M₁.H`/`M₂.H` on `Icc (-1) 1`, yet its docstring (lines 159-161) claims the conclusion is "exactly the negation of `ae_eq_of_forall_mellinMomentH_eq`". That theorem (lines 83-89) carries `h₁ h₂ : IntegrableOn ...`, so as stated the counterexample is not certified to lie in the hypothesis class the positive theorem governs — a reader cannot rule out that the failure is an artifact of inadmissible inputs rather than of using only `N + 1` moments.

summary: The determinacy half and the rank–nullity sharpness half are both faithfully stated and correctly derived; `polynomialModel` is a genuine non-degenerate witness for `GPD.Assumptions`. One gap: the GPD counterexample never asserts that its models satisfy the integrability hypothesis of the determinacy theorem, so it is not certified to live in the class where that theorem applies, which is what its docstring claims.
